commitment: Changes to the course materials this year, newest first. Many of them follow your feedback after class.

releases.title: Lesson 6: focus on the key concepts

items.text: Following your feedback, the Lesson 6 lecture and lab concentrate on the key concepts, so class time goes on understanding them. The wider analysis is in the Notes and the optional Advanced tasks.
The first interactive figure in the Lesson 6 Notes now lets you tilt the cut, and the text beside it is corrected.
An optional derivation in the Lesson 4 Notes shows where the cross-entropy loss comes from.

releases.title: Lesson 6 on the Titanic passenger list

items.text: Lesson 6 (decision trees) now follows the five steps on the Titanic passenger list, with a figure where you drag the tree's depth and watch it overfit.
Both assignments include the University statement on generative AI and ask for a short AI declaration, which is not marked.
Lesson 5 (LDA and QDA) follows the same five steps as the other lessons. Its lab uses a new wine dataset and a data block that stays the same in every later lab.

releases.title: Help with writing the Assignment 1 report

items.text: Optional help with the Assignment 1 report: a short guide, do-and-don't examples, a sample report and a LaTeX template. The brief and the marking are unchanged.
The live classroom can run the two optional assessment workshops.
The home page marks this week's lecture and lab and the next deadline, and each material has one name across the site.
This changelog.
Following feedback on Lab 3, every lab from Lesson 4 comes with a ready-made Colab notebook, and the key modelling decisions are left for you to make.
Lab 4 now includes a task on ROC curves and AUC, and Labs 5–10 are matched to the learning outcomes and a 50-minute session.
The feedback form asks whether the latest change helped.
An optional Kaggle competition for Assignment 1, with an anonymous leaderboard.
One QR code for the live classroom: polls, a question board, “Got it” and “Lost” buttons, and feedback.
A short recap video for each lesson, for revision.
Lessons 3–10 follow the same five steps (problem, model, loss, solution, test), with the mathematics inside each lesson and optional Advanced sections.
Figures in the Lesson 3 Notes now show on the website.
Lesson 2 redesigned around one problem, one loss and one solution, each slide building on the one before.
Pages for Assignments 1 and 2 with deadlines and submission guidance.
Formulas in Lesson 2 now display correctly.
Following feedback after the first class, the Lesson 1 materials are more focused and include new examples. The version taught in class is in the archive.
Advanced investigations and reference solutions in Lab 1.
One-click Colab demos, a public repository of the course materials, and a question board for each class.
One site for every lesson's slides, notes and labs, with anonymous feedback after each class.
Changes after the first year: feedback by QR code during the semester, Q&A before each deadline, more detailed assignment feedback, and lectures combined with computer classes.
This year's redesign adds more mathematics in the lectures and more independent work in the labs.
First run as MAS369 and MAS61007: lectures opening with recent developments in AI, AI-assisted coding in the labs, and assessment by coursework.
